subject: Science
title: The Water Cycle
source: Water Cycle Structured Notes/Study Guide (Crown Jewels 4 Learning) + Science Doodle Notes #24
notes: The study guide says 70% of Earth's surface is water; the doodle notes page says 75%. The app uses the study guide's 70% — please check with her teacher which number the test uses.

lesson.title: A water planet
lesson.html:
About 70% of Earth's surface is covered by water.
Water is stored in oceans, rivers, streams, lakes, ponds and glaciers.

lesson.title: Two kinds of water
lesson.html:
🌊 Salt water ≈ 97% of Earth's water — oceans and some rivers.
🚰 Fresh water ≈ 3% — for drinking — air, soil, rivers, streams, lakes, glaciers.
Most fresh water is frozen in glaciers (big sheets of ice), so we can't use it.

lesson.title: The water cycle
lesson.html: The water cycle is the process by which water moves through the Earth and atmosphere. It is happening constantly, and the sun fuels it.

lesson.title: Four big steps
lesson.html:
☀️ Evaporation – liquid → gas (heat).
☁️ Condensation – gas → liquid droplets (cooling).
🌧️ Precipitation – rain, snow, sleet, hail.
🏞️ Runoff – water flows back to the ocean.
🌱 Transpiration – plants release water vapor (“plant sweat”).

lesson.title: Around and around
lesson.html: Water changes state and then back again — a cycle never stops. Sun heats the ocean → evaporation → condensation → precipitation → runoff → back to the ocean.

list.q: How much of Earth's surface is covered by water?
list.why: About 70% of Earth's surface is covered by water.
list.hint: It's most of the planet — more than half!

list.q: Which is a place where Earth's water is stored?
list.why: Water is stored in oceans, rivers, streams, lakes, ponds and glaciers.

list.q: How many types of water are found on Earth?
list.why: Two types: salt water and fresh water.

list.q: What are the 2 types of water on Earth?
w: Rain water and sea water only
list.why: Salt water and fresh water.

list.q: Which type of water makes up about 97% of Earth's water?
list.why: Salt water is about 97%. Fresh water is only about 3%.

list.q: Fresh water makes up about ___ of Earth's water.
list.why: Fresh water is only about 3% — that's why it's precious.
Salt water is found in oceans and some rivers.

list.a: In the air, soil, rivers, streams, lakes and glaciers
list.why: Fresh water is in the air, soil, rivers, streams, lakes and glaciers.

list.q: Why is most of Earth's fresh water unusable?
w: It is hidden under the ocean
list.why: Most fresh water is frozen in large sheets of ice called glaciers.

list.a: Water changes from one state to another and back again

list.q: What energy source fuels the water cycle?
list.why: The sun's heat powers the water cycle.
list.hint: It shines on the ocean and warms it.

list.q: Which is NOT a kind of precipitation?
list.why: Precipitation is rain, snow, sleet or hail. Evaporation is liquid turning into gas.
Heat makes liquid water change to a gas (water vapor).
Cool air turns water vapor into liquid droplets — clouds!
Rain, snow, sleet and hail.
Heat from the sun makes ocean water rise as water vapor.
Cool air turns the vapor into tiny droplets that make a cloud.
Water droplets fall from the cloud as rain, snow, sleet or hail.
Rain that isn't absorbed by the soil flows back to the ocean.
Plants release water vapor — “plant sweat”.
The sun's heat fuels the whole water cycle.

items.title: Put the water cycle in order
items.why: Evaporation → Condensation → Precipitation → Runoff, then it starts all over again.

items.title: Tell the story of one water drop
steps: Water flows back to the ocean
items.why: The sun heats the ocean, vapor rises, it cools into clouds, falls as precipitation, and runs back to the ocean.
